title: Module objects and the category $\Mod_{\Lambda_X}$
statement:
Let $(\mathcal C,\otimes,\mathbf 1)$ be a monoidal category with associator $\alpha$ and
left unitor $\lambda$. Let $\mathcal R$ be a monoid object of $\mathcal C$, with
multiplication $\mu\colon\mathcal R\otimes\mathcal R\to\mathcal R$ and unit
$\eta\colon\mathbf 1\to\mathcal R$. When $\mathcal C$ is a category of abelian sheaves with
its tensor product, these are the ring objects of [det-def-sfb-ring-object].

1. A *(left) $\mathcal R$-module object* is an object $M$ of $\mathcal C$ with an
   *action* $\gamma_M\colon\mathcal R\otimes M\to M$ that is unital and associative:
   $$
   \gamma_M\circ(\eta\otimes M)=\lambda_M,\qquad
   \gamma_M\circ(\mu\otimes M)=\gamma_M\circ(\mathcal R\otimes\gamma_M)\circ\alpha_{\mathcal R,\mathcal R,M}.
   $$
2. A *morphism of $\mathcal R$-module objects* $f\colon M\to N$ is a morphism of
   $\mathcal C$ with $f\circ\gamma_M=\gamma_N\circ(\mathcal R\otimes f)$. With the
   composition of $\mathcal C$, the $\mathcal R$-module objects form a category
   $\Mod_{\mathcal R}(\mathcal C)$. It has a forgetful functor
   $\Mod_{\mathcal R}(\mathcal C)\to\mathcal C$, $(M,\gamma_M)\mapsto M$. The *regular
   module* is $\mathcal R$ itself with action $\mu$.
3. Let $X$ be a scheme with small pro-étale site $X_{\mathrm{proét}}$
   ([def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]). Give $\Sh(X_{\mathrm{proét}},\Ab)$ the tensor product of
   [lem-weil-pbc-sheaf-tensor-closed]. Let $\Lambda$ be a condensed ring and let
   $\Lambda_X=p_X^*\Lambda$ be its pullback, a ring object of $\Sh(X_{\mathrm{proét}},\Ab)$
   ([det-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients]). The category of *sheaves of
   $\Lambda_X$-modules* is
   $$
   \Mod_{\Lambda_X}:=\Mod_{\Lambda_X}\bigl(\Sh(X_{\mathrm{proét}},\Ab)\bigr).
   $$

proof.text: Apply [det-def-sfb-module-objects-definition] to the given monoidal category $\mathcal C$ and monoid object $(\mathcal R,\mu,\eta)$. Its clauses 1 and 2 give exactly the action, the displayed unit and associativity equations, and the action-commuting morphisms of parts 1 and 2. Its clauses 3 and 4 specify the regular module, the underlying identities and composition, and the object and morphism maps of the forgetful functor. No braiding or commutativity of $\mathcal R$ is required.

source.place: first sentence: module objects, morphisms, regular module and forgetful functor

proof.text: The hypotheses of [det-def-sfb-module-objects-category] are precisely the data just fixed in step 1. Its clause 1 says that identities and composites are module morphisms and that these operations give a category; clause 2 says that forgetting is a faithful functor, in particular a functor; clause 3 verifies the regular module axioms for $(\mathcal R,\mu)$. This supplies all well-definedness assertions in part 2.

source.place: second sentence: category, forgetful functor, regular module

proof.text: For part 3 take $\mathcal C=\Sh(X_{\mathrm{proét}},\Ab)$ with the tensor product of the item (sheafified objectwise $\otimes_{\mathbf Z}$, unit $\underline{\mathbf Z}$) and $\mathcal R=\Lambda_X=p_X^*\Lambda$, which part 3 of the item takes as a ring object, i.e. a monoid object, of this monoidal category. Parts 1 and 2, established in steps 1 and 2 for an arbitrary monoid object of an arbitrary monoidal category, therefore define the category $\Mod_{\Lambda_X}(\Sh(X_{\mathrm{proét}},\Ab))$ for every condensed ring $\Lambda$, with no further hypothesis; in particular no comparison between ring objects and sheaves of rings is used. [det-def-sfb-module-objects-sheaves] is exactly this specialization: it names the same site, the tensor structure $a(\mathcal F\otimes_p\mathcal G)$ with unit $\underline{\mathbf Z}$ (the same structure the item fixes), the pulled-back ring object $\Lambda_X$, and displays $\Mod_{\Lambda_X}=\Mod_{\Lambda_X}(\Sh(X_{\mathrm{proét}},\Ab))$, with abelian-sheaf action maps and action-commuting abelian-sheaf morphisms.

proof_origin.place: complete three-sentence assembly proof, expanded clause by clause
